text: COMITALUS, in law, a county. England was first divided into countries, by counties into hundreds, and there again into tytting, by Alfred the Great. Sometimes it is taken for territory of jurisdiction of a particular place.

parsed.faithful: COMITATUS, in law, a county. England was first divided into counties, the counties into hundreds, and these again into tyfings, by Alfred the Great. Sometimes it is taken for a territory or jurisdiction of a particular place.
parsed.modern: COMITATUS, in law, a county. England was first divided into counties, the counties into hundreds, and these again into tythings, by Alfred the Great. Sometimes it is taken for a territory or jurisdiction of a particular place.
